title: Eventual polynomiality of homogeneous dimensions of a finite standard graded module
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $M=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M_n$ be a finitely generated graded $S$-module: each $M_n$ is a $k$-subspace, the sum is direct, and $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. Then each $M_n$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and there exist $P\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and $n_0\ge0$ such that $\dim_k M_n=P(n)$ for all integers $n\ge n_0$. The polynomial $P$ is allowed to be zero.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, specialized to S_0=k, together with the immediately preceding lemma-graded-module-fg and Example example-K0-field identifying the class of a finite-dimensional k-space with its dimension.

proof.text: Choose degree-one algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ of $S$ as in [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Replace a finite set of module generators by the finite set of all their homogeneous components, denoted $m_j\in M_{d_j}$: their span contains the original generators and hence is $M$. Projecting an expression in these generators onto degree $n$ shows that $M_n$ is spanned over $k$ by $x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_t^{e_t}m_j$ with $\sum_i e_i=n-d_j$. There are finitely many such exponent tuples, including when $t=0$. Thus every $M_n$ is finite-dimensional. The same argument applies to every finite nonnegatively graded module over every standard graded algebra used below.

source.place: Tag 00K0, lemma-graded-module-fg, proof: homogeneous generators and monomials.

proof.text: We prove eventual polynomiality by induction on the size $t$ of a chosen degree-one algebra generating list, simultaneously for all fields, standard graded algebras with at most $t$ such generators, and finite nonnegatively graded modules. The ring $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], applied to the finitely generated $k$-algebra $S$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes every submodule of any finite $S$-module finite. For $t=0$, $S=k$ is concentrated in degree zero, so the homogeneous generators of step 1 imply $M_n=0$ above their finitely many degrees. The zero polynomial proves the base case, also for $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, induction opening; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, and Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation, clause (2).

proof.text: Let $t>0$, assume the induction assertion for $t-1$, and put $x=x_t$. The ideal $xS$ is homogeneous: its degree-$n$ component is $xS_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, and its degree-zero component is zero. Consequently $\overline S=S/xS$ has degree-zero ring $k$ and is generated by the images of $x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}$ in degree one; it is standard graded. Every graded module killed by $x$ is a graded $\overline S$-module. Finite $S$-generators still generate over $\overline S$, so the outer induction applies to every such finite module.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, choice of x and passage to S/(x).

proof.text: First prove the assertion for every finite graded $S$-module $L$ with $x^rL=0$, by induction on $r\ge1$. If $r=1$, step 3 gives the assertion. For $r>1$, $xL$ is a graded submodule generated by $x$ times a finite generating set of $L$, and $L/xL$ is finite and graded. The module $xL$ is killed by $x^{r-1}$ and $L/xL$ is killed by $x$, so both have eventually polynomial homogeneous dimensions by the two induction hypotheses. In each degree the sequence $0\to(xL)_n\to L_n\to(L/xL)_n\to0$ is exact: decompose a representative into homogeneous components to lift a homogeneous quotient element. A basis of $(xL)_n$, together with lifts of a basis of the quotient, is a basis of $L_n$. Thus dimensions add, and the sum of the two eventual polynomials proves the nilpotent case.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, nilpotent case and its short exact sequence.

proof.text: Define $T=\{m\in M:x^r m=0\text{ for some }r\ge1\}$. Sums are killed by a common larger power and scalar multiples remain killed, so $T$ is an $S$-submodule. Since $x$ is homogeneous, $x^rm=0$ implies that each homogeneous component of $m$ is killed by $x^r$, by direct-sum independence. Thus $T$ is graded. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], $T$ has finitely many generators. Choose for each a killing power and take their maximum (take $1$ if $T=0$); then $x^rT=0$. Step 4 supplies an eventual dimension polynomial $P_T$ for $T$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, largest x-power-torsion submodule; uniform exponent from finite generation made explicit.

proof.text: Put $N=M/T$, with its quotient grading. It is finite, and multiplication by $x$ on $N$ is injective: if $xm\in T$, some $x^rxm=0$, hence $m\in T$. Set $C=N/xN$. This is a finite graded module killed by $x$, so step 3 gives a rational polynomial $P_C$ with $\dim_k C_n=P_C(n)$ eventually. For every $n\ge0$, injection by $x$ and the definition of the quotient give $0\to N_n\xrightarrow{x}N_{n+1}\to C_{n+1}\to0$. The homogeneous lifting argument and basis argument from step 4 therefore yield $\dim_k N_{n+1}-\dim_k N_n=\dim_k C_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, x-injective quotient and final displayed sequence.

proof.text: Write $P_C(X)=\sum_{j=0}^d a_j\binom{X}{j}$ with $a_j\in\mathbf Q$: the binomial polynomials have distinct degrees $j$ and nonzero leading coefficients $1/j!$, so coefficient elimination gives this expansion. Put $B(X)=\sum_j a_j\binom{X+1}{j+1}$. Pascal's identity gives $B(n)-B(n-1)=P_C(n)$. Step 6 implies that $\dim_kN_n-B(n)$ has successive differences zero beyond some threshold, hence is constant there by induction on $n$. Adding that rational constant to $B$ gives an eventual polynomial $P_N$ for $\dim_k N_n$.

source.place: Tag 00JZ, lemma-numerical-polynomial, proof of integration using Pascal identity; rational-polynomial version written out.

proof.text: The degreewise exact sequence $0\to T_n\to M_n\to N_n\to0$, with the basis-lifting argument of step 4, gives $\dim_k M_n=\dim_kT_n+\dim_kN_n$. Thus $P=P_T+P_N\in\mathbf Q[X]$ agrees with $\dim_kM_n$ above the maximum of the two thresholds. This closes the induction on $t$. Choose the resulting threshold $n_0\ge0$; step 1 gives finite-dimensionality in every degree, and the construction permits $P=0$, exactly as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, recombination of torsion submodule and x-injective quotient.
